verdicts.title: Complexity Results on DPLL and Resolution
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: DPLL and resolution are two popular methods for solving the problem of propositional satisfiability. Rather than algorithms, they are families of algorithms, as their behavior depend on some choices they face during execution: DPLL depends on the choice of the literal to branch on; resolution depends on the choice of the pair of clauses to resolve at each step. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns the computational complexity of making optimal branching/resolution choices and determining optimal proof sizes (e.g., 'Delta[log]^2-hard', 'NP^PP-hard'), not any spectral/influence-based lower bound on DPLL tree depth. It does not address total influence or clause-indicator Fourier statistics.

verdicts.title: Multiplicative Complexity of Vector Valued Boolean Functions
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We consider the multiplicative complexity of Boolean functions with multiple bits of output, studying how large a multiplicative complexity is necessary and sufficient to provide a desired nonlinearity. For so-called $ΣΠΣ$ circuits, we show that there is a tight connection between error correcting codes and circuits computing functions with high nonlinearity. verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns multiplicative complexity (AND-gate count) of vector-valued Boolean functions and its connection to nonlinearity/error-correcting codes, not total influence, clause-indicator functions, #UNSAT counts, or tree-resolution depth of 3-CNFs.
